transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, well, I'm a secondary school teacher, and I came in because... I just can't seem to... like, I'll sit down with a stack of essays, or a curriculum document, fully intending to work. Which, actually, the school board just completely overhauled our curriculum again. They always do this right in the middle of the term, and my department head is retiring in June so she just forwards us these massive PDFs and doesn't even bother explaining the changes. She's just totally checked out, honestly, and I don't blame her, but it makes it so hard for the rest of us to figure out what we're supposed to be teaching. 

But anyway, yeah, I sit down with the papers, and within ten minutes I realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page. I'm thinking about three completely different things—like whether I need to get my tires rotated, or that documentary I watched last night—and I'm barely taking in a single word of what's actually in front of me.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

No, I don't think so. I'm not really sad or anything. I still like doing my normal stuff, like... I still play my guitar a lot. Actually, I just bought this new loop pedal for it on Saturday. I went down to that little independent music shop on 4th street, and the guy working there—he had this crazy long white beard, looked exactly like a wizard, honestly—he was telling me all about how he used to tour in the 70s with this prog-rock band. I can't remember the name of the band, but he had this whole wild story about their tour bus breaking down in the middle of the desert and they had to hitchhike with all their amps... 

But wait, sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, feeling down. Yeah, no, my mood is mostly fine. I'm just mostly frustrated with the whole staring-at-my-desk thing.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

Tired? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I have a pretty normal amount of energy. I do drink a fair amount of coffee, though. Actually, the coffee situation at work has been a total disaster this week. The staff room espresso machine broke on Tuesday, and Mr. Henderson—he teaches physics—he was absolutely convinced he could fix it himself. He brought in this massive toolbox, like, stuff you'd use on a car engine, and he completely dismantled the thing right on the breakroom table. Just left parts everywhere. And then the bell rang for third period, so he just left it there! People were furious. We had to walk down to the corner store just to get a cup... which, honestly, their coffee is terrible, it always tastes burnt, but you do what you have to do, you know? 

But anyway... wait. Sorry. Did you ask if I was sleeping okay? Or just tired? Yeah, no, physically I feel fine. I'm not lacking energy or anything like that.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough at your job or been blaming yourself for things that aren’t entirely your fault?

Not good enough? Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I actually know I'm a pretty solid teacher. The kids seem to like my classes, mostly. Like, just yesterday, one of my sophomores, Tyler—he's this kid who usually sits in the back and draws these incredibly detailed comic books instead of taking notes. Honestly, his art style is really similar to Jim Lee, if you know him? The guy who did all those X-Men comics back in the 90s. I actually still have a bunch of those in my parents' attic. I really need to go over there and clear those boxes out, my mom has been bugging me about it since Thanksgiving. She wants to turn the space into a sewing room, which is funny because I don't think I've ever seen her sew a single thing in my entire life... 

But wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Blaming myself? Yeah, no. I mean, I get frustrated that I can't just grade the essays when I need to, but I don't feel like I'm a failure or anything. I know I'm good at the actual teaching part.
Outside of work and these curriculum changes, do you often find it hard to focus on tasks or feel easily distracted in other areas of your life?

Yeah, all the time. It's not just the curriculum stuff. Like, that's actually the main reason I came in today. I can sit down with a stack of essays, fully intending to get them done, and within, like, ten minutes, I realize I’ve been staring at the exact same paragraph. And my brain is just... off somewhere else, thinking about three different things at once. I barely take in a single word of what's right in front of me. 

It happens with reading for fun, too. I tried to read this sci-fi novel my brother lent me—he's super into that hard sci-fi stuff, like the really dense physics-heavy ones. He actually just went to this convention in Chicago last month and met one of his favorite authors. He got this signed first edition, which is pretty cool, I guess, though the cover art is kind of cheesy. It's got this weird neon green spaceship that looks like a toaster... I used to have a toaster exactly that color in college. Got it at a thrift store for three bucks. It only toasted on one side, so you had to flip the bread halfway through if you wanted an even crunch...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was the question? Distracted in other areas? Yeah, basically anything where I have to sit still and focus for more than a few minutes, I just zone out.
When did you first start having trouble focusing or getting distracted easily like this?

When did it start? Um... well, it’s been noticeably worse for about 11 months now. That’s when the administration completely changed our curriculum calendar and added all these mandatory after-school planning meetings. 

And honestly, those meetings are just brutal. They put us in the old library, which still has that weird industrial carpeting from the 80s. It’s this awful speckled orange color. It actually reminds me exactly of the carpet in my childhood bedroom. My parents let me pick it out when I was seven, which was a huge mistake in hindsight. I thought orange was the greatest color in the world because of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles—Michelangelo was my favorite. I even had the nunchucks, you know, the little hollow plastic ones? I accidentally broke my older sister's lava lamp with them once while I was practicing in the hallway. Man, she was so mad. It took like three hours to clean up all the oily wax off the floor, and the hallway smelled like fake pine needles for literally months... 

Wait. Sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. What was the question? Oh, when did it start. Right. Yeah, about 11 months ago, when they added the calendar changes and the extra meetings. That's when things really started going downhill for me.
Do you also experience these difficulties with focus and distraction when you're not at work, like at home or in social situations?

At home? Um, yeah, I guess so. I mean, I definitely notice it when I'm trying to do chores or pay bills or whatever. Like, I'll start folding laundry on the couch, and then I'll see the remote and think, oh, I should put on some background noise. So I turn on the TV, and it's on some documentary about, like, deep-sea creatures. And they have those anglerfish, you know? The ones with the little glowing thing on their head? It's crazy how they survive down there with no light. I actually wanted to be a marine biologist when I was a kid, before I realized how much math was involved. I went to this aquarium camp one summer and we got to touch a stingray. It felt super weird, kind of like a wet mushroom. My friend Jake was too scared to do it. He's still like that, actually. We went camping last year and he wouldn't even sleep in the tent because he thought he heard a bear, but it was literally just a raccoon trying to get into our cooler...

Sorry, I'm doing it again. Um, I don't really know if I have that much trouble in social situations? I mean, I talk to my friends fine, I think. But yeah, at home, I definitely get sidetracked a lot.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated, especially when you need to focus on something?

Restless? Um, no, not really. I don't feel like I have to be moving around all the time or anything. I can sit still just fine. I mean, I sit for hours when I'm grading, even if I'm not actually getting anything done. Like, my desk chair is pretty comfortable. I actually splurged on it a couple of years ago because my old one was giving me terrible lower back pain. It's one of those ergonomic ones with the mesh back? I got it during a Black Friday sale online. The shipping was a nightmare, though. The delivery guy left it at the wrong apartment building, and I had to drag this massive heavy box down the street in the rain. It was miserable. And then putting it together took forever because they didn't include the right size Allen wrench in the hardware packet... 

But, uh, anyway. No, I don't really get fidgety or feel like I can't stay seated. I just kind of zone out while I'm sitting there.
Looking back, did you have trouble focusing or staying on task when you were a child, before the age of 12?

As a kid? Um, yeah, actually. I mean, my parents used to get so frustrated with me. Even back in primary school, my report cards would always have those little comments from the teachers saying things like "bright but careless" or "doesn't finish work unless closely supervised." And my backpack was just a disaster zone. My parents were constantly finding all these crumpled-up worksheets at the bottom of it that I had completely forgotten to turn in. 

I actually still have that same problem with bags. Like, my work briefcase right now is full of random stuff. I think there's a half-eaten granola bar in there from last week. It's one of those peanut butter chocolate chip ones. I used to buy the generic brand to save money, but they changed the recipe or something and now they taste like cardboard. So I switched back to the name brand, even though they're way more expensive. It's crazy how much groceries cost right now, honestly. I went to the store just to get coffee and milk the other day, and it was like fifteen dollars. And the line was huge because they only had one cashier working, and the self-checkout machines kept freezing up... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, I definitely had a hard time focusing back then, too. The crumpled worksheets and the teacher comments were pretty much a constant thing.
Have these problems with focusing and getting distracted been happening for at least six months or more?

Six months? Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, it's been noticeably worse for about 11 months now. That's when the school completely changed our curriculum calendar and decided to add these mandatory after-school planning meetings. By the time those meetings start, my brain is just completely drained. And they expect us to sit there and map out these huge unit plans, but all I can focus on is how bad the coffee in the staff lounge is. It's that cheap powdered stuff, you know? It literally tastes like burnt plastic. 

I actually started bringing my own thermos to those meetings. It was this really nice insulated one my sister got me for my birthday. She always gets me the most practical gifts. Like, a couple of years ago, she got me this really heavy-duty ice scraper for my car because I was always just using an old credit card to scrape my windshield in the mornings. Which, by the way, completely ruined the magnetic strip on my card, and I had to order a new one right before a big road trip. We drove all the way up to Maine, and the toll booths wouldn't take Apple Pay, so it was a whole stressful ordeal trying to find loose change under the seats... 

Sorry, I lost my train of thought again. But yes, to answer your question, it's been at least 11 months since it got really bad with the new schedule and the meetings.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, speaking at inappropriate times, or acting without thinking things through?

Interrupting people? Um, no, not really. I mean, I'm pretty quiet in conversations, mostly because I'm usually just trying to follow what people are saying. I don't really blurt things out or do things without thinking. Actually, I tend to overthink things, if anything. Like, if I have to send an email to a parent, I'll sit there staring at the draft for twenty minutes trying to decide if I should use a comma or a semicolon. 

Grammar is so tricky sometimes, even for me, and I teach history. The English teachers get so worked up about it. There's this one teacher, Mrs. Gable, she's retiring next year, and she literally carries around a red pen in the hallway to correct the flyers the kids put up for clubs. She crossed out a misplaced modifier on a poster for the chess club last week. The chess club is actually doing really well this year, though. They made it to the state semi-finals, which is a big deal because our school usually only cares about football. The football boosters bought the team brand new uniforms, but the debate team is still using a buzzer system from the nineties that only works half the time...

Wait, sorry. No, I don't really interrupt people or act impulsively. I mostly just keep to myself.

It's one of those peanut butter chocolate chip ones. I used to buy the generic brand to save money, but they changed the recipe or something and now they taste like cardboard. So I switched back to the name brand, even though they're way more expensive. It's crazy how much groceries cost right now, honestly. I went to the store just to get coffee and milk the other day, and it was like fifteen dollars. And the line was huge because they only had one cashier working, and the self-checkout machines kept freezing up... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, I definitely had a hard time focusing back then, too. The crumpled worksheets and the teacher comments were pretty much a constant thing.

patient.answer:
Six months? Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, it's been noticeably worse for about 11 months now. That's when the school completely changed our curriculum calendar and decided to add these mandatory after-school planning meetings. By the time those meetings start, my brain is just completely drained. And they expect us to sit there and map out these huge unit plans, but all I can focus on is how bad the coffee in the staff lounge is. It's that cheap powdered stuff, you know? It literally tastes like burnt plastic. 

I actually started bringing my own thermos to those meetings. It was this really nice insulated one my sister got me for my birthday. She always gets me the most practical gifts. Like, a couple of years ago, she got me this really heavy-duty ice scraper for my car because I was always just using an old credit card to scrape my windshield in the mornings. Which, by the way, completely ruined the magnetic strip on my card, and I had to order a new one right before a big road trip. We drove all the way up to Maine, and the toll booths wouldn't take Apple Pay, so it was a whole stressful ordeal trying to find loose change under the seats... 

Sorry, I lost my train of thought again. But yes, to answer your question, it's been at least 11 months since it got really bad with the new schedule and the meetings.

inference.note: F06.8 and F06.9 were ruled out as the patient does not report persistent mood symptoms or affective disturbances inconsistent with known physiological effects. The focus remains on persistent difficulty with attention and distractibility, both in childhood and currently, supporting F48.0 (ADHD) and possibly F34.1 (Persistent Mild Mood Disorder) due to ongoing stressors.

patient.answer:
Interrupting people? Um, no, not really. I mean, I'm pretty quiet in conversations, mostly because I'm usually just trying to follow what people are saying. I don't really blurt things out or do things without thinking. Actually, I tend to overthink things, if anything. Like, if I have to send an email to a parent, I'll sit there staring at the draft for twenty minutes trying to decide if I should use a comma or a semicolon. 

Grammar is so tricky sometimes, even for me, and I teach history. The English teachers get so worked up about it. There's this one teacher, Mrs. Gable, she's retiring next year, and she literally carries around a red pen in the hallway to correct the flyers the kids put up for clubs. She crossed out a misplaced modifier on a poster for the chess club last week. The chess club is actually doing really well this year, though. They made it to the state semi-finals, which is a big deal because our school usually only cares about football. The football boosters bought the team brand new uniforms, but the debate team is still using a buzzer system from the nineties that only works half the time...

Wait, sorry. No, I don't really interrupt people or act impulsively. I mostly just keep to myself.

No features of persistent depressive disorder (F34.1) are present, as mood remains euthymic and the primary issue is attentional rather than affective.
